headline: Elementary school planners advanced Option 3 to schematic design, while town committees weighed major capital requests, potential budget cuts, and development proposals.
synopsis: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance Option 3 to schematic design for detailed cost estimates, while the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed up to $49 million in bondable requests dominated by the Neary School project. Facing potential municipal budget constraints, the Board of Health approved an alternate level-funded budget plan that would force Friday office closures and delay septic reviews if an operating override fails. The Planning Board extended its review timeline for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco application to December, and the Zoning Board of Appeals prepared town zoning updates to comply with state law while shelving further local action on two-family housing. Additionally, the Wastewater Study Committee approved a pro bono partnership with Artefacts AI to assess local parcels for wastewater disposal.

highlights.title: Option 3 advanced for elementary school building project
highlights.why: The committee voted 4-0 to direct Tappé Architects to develop schematic designs and detailed cost estimates for Option 3, focusing the project's next design phase while keeping final recommendations open.

highlights.title: Health Department details service cuts if town override fails
highlights.why: The board approved an alternate level-funded FY28 budget scenario that would result in Friday health office closures, septic review delays of up to two weeks, and potential elimination of town flu clinics if an operating override is not approved.

highlights.title: Capital requests review includes $45 million Neary School placeholder
highlights.why: The committee reviewed initial FY28 capital requests totaling $2.152 million in direct appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable items, which is heavily dominated by a $45 million placeholder for the Neary School building project.

highlights.title: Costco hearing continued as decision deadline extends to December
highlights.why: The Planning Board voted to continue public hearings for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco project to a special November 2 meeting and extended its statutory decision deadline to December 18 while traffic peer reviews are completed.

highlights.title: Zoning amendments drafted to align with state Chapter 40A
highlights.why: Staff presented draft zoning bylaw amendments adjusting nonconforming lot and structure rules, extending abandonment timelines, and altering variance criteria to conform with revised state statutes ahead of the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Pro bono AI study approved for wastewater site selection
highlights.why: The committee voted to collaborate with Artefacts AI at no cost to Southborough to evaluate land parcels and hydrologic percolation data for potential municipal wastewater disposal sites.

looking_ahead.what: Planning Board special meeting regarding Costco (21 Coslin Drive), Fay School as-builts, 361 Turnpike Road temporary occupancy, and 2027 meeting schedule
